data.detailed_description: Embark on a "Climate Walk" Trek in Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary! Discover the diverse ecosystems of Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary on our unique "Climate Walk" trekking program. This challenging yet rewarding journey will take you through various climatic zones within this biodiversity hotspot, offering an immersive experience in the heart of the Western Ghats. Trek Details: Distance: 12 km Duration: 7 hours Difficulty: Moderate to Hard Starting Time: 7:00 AM Experience the Sanctuary: Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary, located in Thrissur district, Kerala, is a haven of lush tropical rainforests, teeming with a rich array of flora and fauna. As you trek through different elevations, you'll witness the subtle shifts in vegetation and climate, from moist deciduous forests to tropical evergreen patches. Keep an eye out for diverse wildlife, including various bird species (over 160 recorded!), vibrant butterflies, and perhaps even glimpses of larger mammals. Our experienced guides will lead you through the trails, sharing insights into the sanctuary's ecological significance. Inclusions: Your trek package ensures a comfortable and enriching experience: Sanctuary Entry Fee Breakfast Mineral Water Snacks Lunch Booking Information: Ticket Charge: ₹1000/- per person Minimum Requirement: 10 persons (or a minimum payment of ₹10000/-) Pre-booking is essential. To book your "Climate Walk" adventure, please call: 8547603459 Prepare for an unforgettable journey through the natural wonders of Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary!
data.description: Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary, nestled in the Western Ghats of Thrissur district is a hidden gem for nature lovers. This pristine sanctuary boasts lush tropical rainforests, cascading waterfalls, and diverse wildlife, making it a perfect destination for trekking, birdwatching, and wildlife spotting. The sanctuary is home to dense evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, providing a habitat for a variety of flora and fauna. Visitors can enjoy trekking, cycling, turtle ride, offered by the Kerala Forest Department.
